title: Moong Dal Vada / Gâteau Piment
subtitle: Fried lentil fritters, two ways — Indian moong dal vada or Mauritian gâteau piment.
protein: ~10–12g protein per adult serving — from moong dal or split peas

nightPrep.label: Night Before — pick your version
items: Indian moong dal vada: soak {@dal|yellow moong dal (split, skinned)} 2–3 hours
Mauritian gâteau piment: soak {@dal|yellow split peas} 8–12 hours — they need much longer
Drain well before grinding

items.name: Moong dal or split peas, soaked

method.title: Grind and season the base
items: Drain the soaked {@dal|dal or split peas} well — split peas feel firmer than dal even after a long soak
Add to a blender with {@ginger} and {@salt:grind|salt}

Pulse to a coarse, thick paste — no added water; batter should hold its shape on a spoon. Split peas grind a bit coarser than moong dal — a few small flecks are normal and give gâteau piment its characteristic bite.
Too wet? Add a spoon of chickpea flour. Too dry? A few drops of water at a time.
Transfer to a mixing bowl; mix in {@hing}, {@cumin}, {@coriander-seeds} and {@turmeric}
Mix in {@salt:season|the remaining salt} — this is the shared base, no chili has gone in yet

method.label: Toddler portion — pull now
items: Scoop out about ⅓ cup of the seasoned base into a separate bowl before any chili is added
Fold in {@potato:toddler} and {@ghee-batter:toddler} to soften the texture
Set aside — this bowl stays out of all remaining adult steps

method.title: Spice and fry the adult batch
items: Into the remaining base, mix {@green-chili}, your herb — {@curry-leaves} for the Indian version, or {@thyme} for Mauritian — and {@cilantro}
Heat {@oil} in a kadai or heavy pot over medium-high heat
Wet hands, shape adult batter into small flat patties {=~2 tbsp each} — for gâteau piment, shape slightly thicker in the center than a typical vada
Fry in batches until deep golden and firm — 3–4 minutes per side for moong dal, 4–5 minutes for split peas, which take a little longer to cook through
Drain on a rack or paper towel

method.title: Cook the toddler patties
items: Heat {@ghee-pan:toddler} in a small nonstick pan over medium-low heat
Shape the toddler batter into 3–4 small, thin patties (thinner than the adult ones, for a soft bite)
Pan-sear 2–3 minutes per side until set through and lightly golden — no raw batter should remain
Cool and cut into soft strips before serving to reduce choking risk

method.label: Notes
method.text: These are culinary cousins — both trace back to Indian indentured-labor cooking traditions, but diverged: Indian moong dal vada uses skinned split mung bean and curry leaves; Mauritian gâteau piment traditionally uses yellow split peas and thyme (often chives too, swapped here for cilantro to keep it Jain). Toor dal isn't offered as a third option — it's too soft and crumbly to hold together fried this way. Lighter version: brush patties with oil and air-fry in the Ninja Crispi at 350°F for 8–10 minutes, flipping halfway — add 2–3 minutes for split peas, and check early since the Crispi runs hot; toddler patties stay pan-seared, their thin shape dries out in the Crispi. Leftover vadas keep 3 days refrigerated and re-crisp in a dry pan, or the Crispi at 330°F for 3–4 minutes.
